editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the version-compatibility caveat (build against v2.4.0 → runtime v2.4.1 guaranteed, v2.5.0 may break), the `static`-linkage rationale, the "borrow" semantics of `qk_*_convert_from_python` (mutations propagate, don't drop your reference), the `PyInit__core` double-underscore rule and the `qk_import()` criticality are all rendered accurately, and register stays informal singular throughout (يمكنك، ابدأ، اكتب، إذا كنت مهتماً). What a native technical editor would change: (1) software "port" is rendered as منفذاً ("outlet / access point") twice, a false friend; Arabic uses نقل/تحويل إلى C, and منفذ nudges the reader toward "an entry point to the pass" rather than "a re-implementation of it". (2) "performance-critical sections" is mis-parsed in the opening as الأجزاء الحرجة من الأداء ("the critical parts of the performance"), while the same idea is rendered correctly later as الكود الحرج من حيث الأداء — one wrong parse plus an internal inconsistency. (3) Smaller slips: "it is instructive to use a meaningful transpiler pass" softened to يُستحسن ("it is advisable"); "propagates the error" as تُشيع الخطأ (تُمرّر/تنقل is the technical verb); the calqued "(this is standard)" → (هذا معيار) instead of (وهذا هو المعتاد); and the pronoun mismatch in الذي يُشكّل قاعدتهم for "the Python object that backs them". None of these would mislead a learner about the C-extension mechanics.

examples.source: The package provides a simple port of `AddSpectatorMeasures` from the Qiskit addons to C. … This guide produces a simple port of that pass
examples.suggested: تُقدّم الحزمة نسخة منقولة بسيطة إلى C من `AddSpectatorMeasures` … ينتج هذا الدليل نقلاً بسيطاً لتلك التمريرة إلى C
examples.translation: تُقدّم الحزمة منفذاً بسيطاً لـ `AddSpectatorMeasures` من إضافات Qiskit إلى C. … ينتج هذا الدليل منفذاً بسيطاً لتلك التمريرة
examples.why: منفذ is the false-friend reading of "port" (outlet / harbour / network port). Arabic software usage for porting code is نقل / تحويل. As written the reader can parse it as "an access point to the pass" rather than "a re-implementation of the pass in C"; surrounding context rescues it, so imperfect-but-recognizable rather than misleading.

examples.source: You can write performance-critical sections of your Qiskit extensions in C … / all the performance-critical code of our package
examples.suggested: يمكنك كتابة الأجزاء الحرجة من حيث الأداء في امتدادات Qiskit
examples.translation: يمكنك كتابة الأجزاء الحرجة من الأداء في امتدادات Qiskit … / كل الكود الحرج من حيث الأداء في حزمتنا
examples.why: The first instance mis-parses the compound: الأجزاء الحرجة من الأداء reads as "the critical parts of the performance". The later instance (الحرج من حيث الأداء) is the correct rendering, so the same concept is split two ways within the file.

examples.source: it is instructive to use a meaningful transpiler pass for the demonstration
examples.suggested: إذ من المفيد تعليمياً استخدام تمريرة ترانسبايلر ذات معنى للإيضاح
examples.translation: إذ يُستحسن استخدام تمريرة ترانسبايلر ذات معنى للإيضاح
examples.why: "Instructive" (pedagogically informative) becomes يُستحسن ("it is advisable/preferable"), converting a statement about teaching value into a recommendation. Harmless to the technical content but flattens the authorial intent.

examples.source: If this fails, the function propagates the error. / (this is standard) / the Python object that backs them
examples.suggested: إذا فشل ذلك، تُمرّر الدالة الخطأ. / (وهذا هو المعتاد) / كائن Python الذي يدعمها
examples.translation: إذا فشل هذا، تُشيع الدالة الخطأ. / (هذا معيار) / كائن Python الذي يُشكّل قاعدتهم
examples.why: تُشيع means "circulates/spreads (news)", not error propagation; (هذا معيار) is a calque of "this is standard" that reads as "this is a standard"; and قاعدتهم uses a masculine-human plural pronoun for the C handles instead of the non-human ـها. All stiff/robotic rather than wrong.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the course list, the "at or beyond an advanced undergraduate level" qualifier (مناسب لمن هم في مستوى الدراسة الجامعية المتقدمة أو ما بعدها), and the entire Credly privacy notice are all rendered faithfully, and the informal singular register holds throughout (مرحبًا بك، أجرِ الاختبار، بعد اجتيازك). Three things a native technical editor would still change: "superdense coding" is rendered "الترميز الفائق", which drops the "dense" component — the conventional Arabic is "الترميز فائق الكثافة" (the parenthesized English keeps it recognizable, so it does not mislead); "lecture notes" is calqued as "الملاحظات المحاضراتية", a construction no Arabic technical writer would use (مذكّرات المحاضرات / ملاحظات المحاضرات); and "a few among many" becomes the stilted "بعض من كثيرٍ يُغطّي هذه المادة". Also note both "Basics of quantum information" and "Fundamentals of quantum algorithms" collapse to "أساسيات", losing the distinction between the two sibling course titles, though this is defensible in Arabic.

examples.source: superdense coding
examples.suggested: الترميز فائق الكثافة (Superdense Coding)
examples.translation: الترميز الفائق (Superdense Coding)
examples.why: "الفائق" renders only "super" and drops "dense"; the established Arabic term is "فائق الكثافة". Recognizable thanks to the parenthesized English, so MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: The first chapter of these lecture notes includes a more formal and detailed introduction to sets and functions.
examples.suggested: يتضمن الفصل الأول من مذكّرات المحاضرات هذه مقدمة أكثر رسمية وتفصيلًا للمجموعات والدوال.
examples.translation: يتضمن الفصل الأول من هذه الملاحظات المحاضراتية مقدمة أكثر رسمية وتفصيلًا للمجموعات والدوال.
examples.why: "الملاحظات المحاضراتية" is a word-for-word calque of "lecture notes"; the adjectival form المحاضراتية is not idiomatic Arabic. A native writer uses the idafa مذكّرات/ملاحظات المحاضرات.

examples.source: The following sources are a few among many that cover this material:
examples.suggested: المصادر التالية قليل من مصادر كثيرة تُغطّي هذه المادة:
examples.translation: المصادر التالية هي بعض من كثيرٍ يُغطّي هذه المادة:
examples.why: "بعض من كثيرٍ" is a literal transposition of "a few among many" with a dangling indefinite noun; reads as translationese rather than written Arabic. Meaning is intact.

examples.source: Basics of quantum information … Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.suggested: أساسيات معلومات الكم … مبادئ خوارزميات الكم
examples.translation: أساسيات معلومات الكم … أساسيات خوارزميات الكم
examples.why: Both sibling course titles collapse to أساسيات, erasing the Basics/Fundamentals distinction the series uses to name two different courses. Defensible in Arabic and not misleading, so at most MINOR.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the batch/session/job tradeoffs, the "up to five classical jobs in parallel" figure, the device-drift caveat in the variational example, and the stale-noise-model caveat for PEA/PEC all survive intact, and informal register (استخدم/يمكنك/عبء عملك) is consistent. The main editorial problem is a term collision: "functionality" is rendered وظائف ("جميع وظائف وضع الدُّفعة", "الوظائف الإضافية التي توفرها الجلسات") in a file where وظيفة is the established rendering of "job", so those two lines momentarily read as "all the batch-mode jobs" / "the additional jobs sessions provide"; line 36 gets it right with المزايا الإضافية, so it is also internally inconsistent — إمكانات/خصائص would fix both. Secondary: "fixed overhead" becomes "تكلفة ثابتة" (fixed cost) in a page that elsewhere uses تكلفة for money (أقل تكلفة / أغلى تكلفةً), where عبء ثابت is meant; "as closely together as possible" is rendered two different ways, and the second one ("تعمل في أقرب وقت ممكن من بعضها") flirts with "as soon as possible"; and the frontmatter description subordinates batch and single jobs under sessions instead of listing the three modes in parallel. None of these teach a false concept, so this stays short of FAIL.

examples.source: All the functionality from batch mode (but requiring increased usage…) / …whenever you don't need the additional functionality sessions provides.
examples.suggested: جميع إمكانات وضع الدُّفعة … / … الإمكانات الإضافية التي توفرها الجلسات.
examples.translation: جميع وظائف وضع الدُّفعة (مع الحاجة إلى استخدام أعلى…) / …لا تحتاج فيها إلى الوظائف الإضافية التي توفرها الجلسات.
examples.why: وظيفة is this file's word for "job" (وظائف بدائية، إرسال وظائف متعددة), so using وظائف for "functionality" makes both lines momentarily parse as "all the batch-mode jobs" and "the extra jobs sessions provide". Line 36 already renders the same idea correctly as المزايا الإضافية للجلسات, so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: There is a fixed overhead associated with running a job.
examples.suggested: هناك عبء ثابت (overhead) مرتبط بتشغيل أي وظيفة.
examples.translation: هناك تكلفة ثابتة مرتبطة بتشغيل أي وظيفة.
examples.why: The overhead here is time, and the very next clause measures it in QPU time. But this page uses تكلفة for monetary expense elsewhere (أقل تكلفة بشكل عام مقارنة بالجلسات، الجلسات أغلى تكلفةً), so "تكلفة ثابتة" invites reading it as a fixed per-job charge.

examples.source: it's beneficial that they run as closely together as possible
examples.suggested: يُستحسن أن تعمل بأقصى قدر من التقارب الزمني فيما بينها
examples.translation: يُستحسن أن تعمل في أقرب وقت ممكن من بعضها
examples.why: "في أقرب وقت ممكن" is the fixed Arabic idiom for "as soon as possible"; only the trailing من بعضها rescues the intended "close to each other". The session bullet already uses the clean phrasing بأقصى قدر من التقارب الزمني — reusing it would be both natural and consistent.

examples.source: Choose the right execution mode for Qiskit Runtime sessions, batch, or single jobs.
examples.suggested: اختر وضع التنفيذ المناسب في Qiskit Runtime: الجلسات أو الدُّفعات أو الوظائف الفردية.
examples.translation: اختر وضع التنفيذ المناسب لجلسات Qiskit Runtime، سواء كان دُفعة أو وظائف فردية.
examples.why: The English lists three coordinate execution modes; the Arabic makes "sessions" the head noun and demotes batch and single jobs to sub-varieties of a session ("سواء كان دُفعة أو وظائف فردية"), which inverts the page's own taxonomy in the search/meta description.

editor_note: The lesson's entire closing paragraph is missing from the Arabic file: the EN source ends with "Although there's randomness involved, the statistics are very unlikely to deviate too much after 1000 runs. The quantum strategy wins about 85% of the time while a classical strategy can't win more than about 75% of the time." The Arabic file simply stops after the ```text Fraction of games won: 0.747``` block (line 1106). This drops both the statistical caveat (that 0.867 / 0.747 are sampling estimates over 1000 runs, not exact values) and the headline 85%-vs-75% conclusion the whole CHSH section builds toward — an Arabic learner is left with two bare printed numbers and no interpretation. Secondary, non-misleading slips: "a unitary qubit gate" is rendered "بوابة كيوبت وحيدة" (= single/sole gate) at line 87 although "unitary" is correctly "أحادية" everywhere else (line 493); "arbitrary" becomes "اختياريتان" (= optional) at line 803 where "اعتباطيتان/كيفيّتان" is meant, and the source's "interesting" is upgraded to "بالغ الأهمية" (= extremely important) twice (lines 384, 778). Terminology is also split within the file: quantum = كمية vs كمومية (lines 43/180/941 vs 435/547/579), and "standard basis" = الأساس القياسي (line 193) vs الأساس المعياري (lines 563, 577), the latter colliding with "معياري" used for orthonormal at line 804.

examples.source: Although there's randomness involved, the statistics are very unlikely to deviate too much after 1000 runs. The quantum strategy wins about 85% of the time while a classical strategy can't win more than about 75% of the time.
examples.suggested: رغم وجود العشوائية، من غير المرجح أبدًا أن تنحرف الإحصاءات كثيرًا بعد 1000 تشغيل. تفوز الاستراتيجية الكمومية نحو 85% من المرات، بينما لا تستطيع أي استراتيجية كلاسيكية الفوز بأكثر من نحو 75% من المرات.
examples.translation: (entirely absent — the Arabic file ends after the ```text Fraction of games won: 0.747``` code block)
examples.why: The lesson's concluding paragraph — carrying both the caveat that the printed 0.867/0.747 are stochastic estimates and the 85%-vs-75% punchline that the entire CHSH section was built to demonstrate — is missing. The Arabic learner sees two raw numbers with no interpretation and no warning about statistical fluctuation, so the demonstration's conclusion is never stated.

examples.source: First we'll randomly choose a unitary qubit gate.
examples.suggested: أولًا، سنختار بوابة كيوبت أحادية (unitary) بشكل عشوائي.
examples.translation: أولًا، سنختار بوابة كيوبت وحيدة بشكل عشوائي.
examples.why: "unitary" is rendered "وحيدة" (single/sole), which reads as "single-qubit gate" and loses the unitarity property that the whole inverse-gate verification argument depends on. The file itself uses the correct "أحادية" for unitary at line 493 (مصفوفة أحادية), so this is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: before that let us briefly acknowledge that it's also interesting to consider other nonlocal games. In fact, it's extremely interesting;
examples.suggested: لكن قبل ذلك دعنا نُقر بإيجاز بأن من المثير للاهتمام أيضًا النظر في ألعاب غير محلية أخرى. بل إنه مثير للاهتمام إلى حد بعيد؛
examples.translation: لكن قبل ذلك دعونا نُقر بأن دراسة ألعاب غير محلية أخرى أمر بالغ الأهمية أيضًا. في الواقع، الأمر مثير للاهتمام بشكل مذهل؛
examples.why: "interesting" is upgraded to "بالغ الأهمية" (of great importance), which both strengthens the claim and breaks the rhetorical escalation into the next sentence ("In fact, it's extremely interesting") — the Arabic now says "important… in fact interesting", which reads as a non-sequitur. The same swap recurs at line 778 ("a very interesting example" → "بالغ الأهمية"). "briefly" is also dropped.

examples.source: For the moment, though, let's take α and β to be arbitrary.
examples.suggested: في الوقت الحالي، لنفترض أن $\alpha$ و$\beta$ قيمتان كيفيّتان (اعتباطيتان).
examples.translation: في الوقت الحالي، لنفترض أن $\alpha$ و$\beta$ قيمتان اختياريتان.
examples.why: "اختياريتان" means "optional", not "arbitrary"; the point is that the derivation holds for any values of the two angles, not that supplying them is optional. The file already uses the correct word "اعتباطيًا" for "arbitrary" at line 239.

examples.source: Here is a quantum circuit implementation of the teleportation protocol.
examples.suggested: هذا تطبيق بدائرة كمية لبروتوكول النقل الكمي.
examples.translation: هذا تطبيق بدائر كمية لبروتوكول النقل الكمي.
examples.why: "بدائر" is not a valid form — the singular is "دائرة" and the plural "دوائر"; the intended reading is "بدائرة كمية". A stray typo in the very first prose sentence of the page. Compare also line 804 "أساساً متعامداً ومعياراً", where "معيارياً" (orthonormal) is written as the noun "معيارًا" (a criterion).

editor_note: Faithful and idiomatic across all four prose passages: the BackendV2 condition (طالما أنه يُطبِّق واجهة BackendV2), the Estimator caveat (لا تقدم أي تطبيق لتخفيف أخطاء القياس أو البوابات "جاهزًا للاستخدام"، إذ صُمِّمت... للتشغيل محليًا على جهاز المستخدم) and the Sampler requirement (يتطلب Backend يدعم خيار memory) all keep their negation, causality and force; error mitigation→تخفيف الأخطاء and class→الفئة are correct and consistent, with idiomatic غير أنّ rather than a calqued لكن.

Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing technical claims all survive intact (break-even/9-qubit Shor comparison, "just the locations are independent but the actual errors may be correlated", "logical qubits are *never* exposed", the below-threshold conclusion), and core terms are correct and consistent (fault tolerance→التسامح مع الأخطاء, unitary→وحدوية, qubit→كيوبت, decoherence→إزالة الترابط، surface code→رمز السطح). Four editorial slips remain: (1) "it is certainly reasonable to object to such a model" is hedged down to "قد يبدو من المعقول الاعتراض" ("it may seem reasonable"), weakening the author's own endorsement of the objection; (2) "gadgets" is over-translated as "الأجهزة الصغيرة" ("small devices"), which nudges a learner toward hardware rather than circuit sub-blocks — it is glossed with (gadgets) at first use and used consistently, so it stays recognizable; (3) two agreement/number errors — "الأخطاء والعطل" (should be الأعطال), and "يتراكم الإنتروبيا … لإزالته" mixing masculine agreement on the feminine الإنتروبيا, plus the clunky تراكم/يتراكم repetition in the same clause; (4) stiff calques: "تمثل المثال المثالي" for "represents an ideal" and "يُربط … احتمالات حدوث أشياء خاطئة متنوعة" for "probabilities for various things to go wrong" (also should be تُربط). Additionally the DefinitionTooltip definition text for entropy is left in English and is user-visible.

examples.source: Now, it is certainly reasonable to object to such a model, because there probably will be correlations among errors in real physical devices.
examples.suggested: ومن المعقول تمامًا الاعتراض على مثل هذا النموذج، لأنه ...
examples.translation: قد يبدو من المعقول الاعتراض على مثل هذا النموذج، لأنه في أجهزة فيزيائية حقيقية سيكون ثمة على الأرجح ترابط بين الأخطاء.
examples.why: 'certainly reasonable' is an endorsement; 'قد يبدو من المعقول' ('it may seem reasonable') turns it into a merely apparent objection the author might not share. The following 'لا أحد ينكر ذلك' still rescues the point, so it does not mislead outright, but the stance is softened.

examples.source: …are performed by so-called *gadgets*, which could each involve multiple qubits and multiple operations.
examples.suggested: بل تُنفَّذ عبر ما يُسمى *الأدوات* (gadgets) / أو الإبقاء على gadgets كما هي
examples.translation: بل تُنفَّذ عبر ما يُسمى *الأجهزة الصغيرة* (gadgets)، التي قد تتضمن كل منها كيوبتات متعددة وعمليات متعددة.
examples.why: A gadget here is a circuit sub-block, not a device; 'الأجهزة الصغيرة' ('small devices') pushes the learner toward hardware. It is glossed in English at first use and applied consistently, so the concept stays identifiable — imperfect but recognizable.

examples.source: As errors take place, entropy builds up, and constant work is required to remove it from the system…
examples.suggested: ومع وقوع الأخطاء تتراكم الإنتروبيا، ويلزم عمل مستمر لإزالتها من النظام…
examples.translation: مع تراكم الأخطاء، يتراكم الإنتروبيا، ويتطلب الأمر عملًا مستمرًا لإزالته من النظام…
examples.why: Gender agreement is wrong twice (يتراكم / لإزالته on the feminine الإنتروبيا), and تراكم/يتراكم repeat in adjacent clauses where the English has 'take place' then 'builds up'. A native technical writer would not leave this.

examples.source: …a precise mathematical model — a *noise model* — through which *probabilities* for various things to go wrong can be associated.
examples.suggested: …تُربط من خلاله *احتمالات* لأن تسوء أمور مختلفة.
examples.translation: …نموذج رياضي دقيق — *نموذج ضوضاء* — يُربط من خلاله *احتمالات* حدوث أشياء خاطئة متنوعة.
examples.why: 'أشياء خاطئة' is a calque of 'things wrong' and reads as machine output; also the verb should agree (تُربط, not يُربط) with the plural احتمالات.

examples.source: A circuit like this one represents an ideal, and an actual implementation of it won't be perfect.
examples.suggested: دائرة كهذه تمثل حالة مثالية، وأي تنفيذ فعلي لها لن يكون مثاليًا.
examples.translation: دائرة كهذه تمثل المثال المثالي، والتطبيق الفعلي لها لن يكون مثاليًا.
examples.why: 'an ideal' (the noun) becomes 'المثال المثالي' — redundant and stiff, and it collides awkwardly with the 'مثال' (example) used in the preceding paragraph for the teleportation circuit.

editor_note: Meaning is essentially faithful throughout this short page and nothing hallucinated; the frontmatter even preserves the upstream "Estimator primitive" wording rather than silently "fixing" it. Three editorial slips: (1) the note "Not all options work together on all types of circuits" is rendered "لا تعمل جميع الخيارات معًا على جميع أنواع…", which in Arabic reads more naturally as عموم النفي ("none of the options work together") rather than the intended partial negation — "ليست كل الخيارات متوافقة معًا…" would be unambiguous; context (the example enabling DD + twirling together) rescues it, so this is a clarity slip rather than a true inversion. (2) "dynamical decoupling" is rendered "الفصل الديناميكي" (lit. "dynamic separation"); the conventional domain rendering is "فك الاقتران الديناميكي" — recognizable but imprecise. (3) "achieve a balance between perfecting your results" is softened to "تحسين النتائج" (improving), losing the "perfecting" end-of-spectrum contrast that motivates the trade-off. Register is correctly informal singular throughout (تعرَّف، استكشف، اختر، مهمتك), and "error mitigation and suppression" is rendered consistently as "تخفيف الأخطاء وتثبيطها" in both body and link text.

examples.source: Not all options work together on all types of circuits.
examples.suggested: ليست كل الخيارات متوافقة معًا على جميع أنواع الدوائر.
examples.translation: لا تعمل جميع الخيارات معًا على جميع أنواع الـ Circuits.
examples.why: Arabic "لا + جميع" defaults to total negation (no option works with any other), not the English partial negation. The surrounding example (DD + gate twirling enabled together) contradicts that reading, so a learner is likely to recover the intent, but the sentence as written points the wrong way.

examples.source: dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: فك الاقتران الديناميكي
examples.translation: الفصل الديناميكي
examples.why: "الفصل" means separation/partition; the technique decouples the qubit from its environment. The conventional Arabic domain rendering is "فك الاقتران الديناميكي". Recognizable, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would change it.

examples.source: it is important to achieve a balance between perfecting your results and ensuring that your job completes in a reasonable amount of time
examples.suggested: … توازن بين إتقان النتائج إلى أقصى حد والتأكد من إتمام مهمتك في وقت معقول
examples.translation: من المهم تحقيق توازن بين تحسين النتائج والتأكد من إتمام مهمتك في وقت معقول
examples.why: "perfecting" is softened to "تحسين" (merely improving). The English deliberately names the extreme end of the trade-off — that is what makes the balance non-trivial; the Arabic flattens the pedagogical contrast.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the directionally load-bearing statements all survive correctly: "tensor factor on the right" → «العامل التنسوري على اليمين», the CX control/target assignment is NOT swapped («الكيوبت اليسرى هي كيوبت التحكم والكيوبت اليمنى هي كيوبت الهدف»), the "it is *not* referring to the right-most or left-most qubit" caveat is kept, and qubit-0 = rightmost with Qiskit's right-to-left numbering is intact; no hallucinated claims, informal register (لاحظ، إليك) holds. Four editorial slips remain: (1) «وكذلك، كما في حالة المتجهات، تُكافئ عملية `^` تماماً» is grammatically dangling — تُكافئ is transitive and has no object, a native writer would put «فإن عملية `^` مكافئة لها تماماً»; (2) "Bell state" is transliterated «حالة بل», and بل is a very common Arabic particle ("rather/but"), so it reads as a stray function word — the conventional form is «حالة بيل»; (3) كيوبت switches grammatical gender within the file, feminine in the CX paragraph («الكيوبت اليسرى/اليمنى») but masculine elsewhere («الكيوبت الأيمن أو الأيسر», «الكيوبت الأقصى يميناً»); (4) "the plus and minus states" becomes «للحالتين الموجبة والسالبة», which reads as "positive and negative states" rather than the |+⟩/|−⟩ basis states. None of these would make a learner form a false belief — the concepts stay identifiable from the adjacent labels and math.

examples.source: Again, like in the vector case, the `^` operation is equivalent.
examples.suggested: وكذلك، كما في حالة المتجهات، فإن عملية `^` مكافئة لها تماماً.
examples.translation: وكذلك، كما في حالة المتجهات، تُكافئ عملية `^` تماماً.
examples.why: تُكافئ is transitive in Arabic and is left without an object, so the sentence dangles; the English ellipsis does not carry over. A native technical writer would use the adjectival مكافئة لها.

examples.source: The result is the Bell state $\vert\phi^{+}\rangle.$
examples.suggested: والنتيجة هي حالة بيل $\vert\phi^{+}\rangle$.
examples.translation: والنتيجة هي حالة بل $\vert\phi^{+}\rangle$.
examples.why: «بل» is a high-frequency Arabic particle meaning "rather/but", so «حالة بل» momentarily parses as a conjunction rather than the physicist's name; the established Arabic transliteration of Bell is «بيل».

examples.source: the left-hand qubit is the control and the right-hand qubit is the target / the right-most or left-most qubit / which is the rightmost qubit
examples.suggested: Pick one gender for كيوبت across the file (masculine الكيوبت الأيسر/الأيمن is used in the majority of the file).
examples.translation: الكيوبت اليسرى … الكيوبت اليمنى (fem.) vs الكيوبت الأيمن أو الأيسر … الكيوبت الأقصى يميناً (masc.)
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency in the grammatical gender of the core term كيوبت; harmless to comprehension but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: Other allowed labels include "+" and "-" for the plus and minus states
examples.suggested: … للحالتين الزائد والناقص (أو: لحالتَي $\vert+\rangle$ و$\vert-\rangle$)
examples.translation: تشمل التسميات المسموح بها أيضاً "+" و"-" للحالتين الموجبة والسالبة
examples.why: «الموجبة والسالبة» reads as "positive and negative states", which is not the domain concept; the intended referent is the |+⟩/|−⟩ basis states. Recoverable from the adjacent "+"/"-" labels, hence minor.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, number, caveat and hedge in the source survives intact (the "optimal / no method can achieve a smaller measurement overhead" claim, the "noise can fluctuate and drift ... might result in inaccurate results" caveat, and the 0.18409094298943401 noiseless value are all faithful), and the informal register holds throughout (قم بالمصادقة، أنك قد حفظت حسابك، يمكنك استرجاع). The defects are terminological. "observable" is rendered as المراقِب / المراقِبات with an explicit kasra — the active participle, i.e. "the observer" rather than the observed quantity; a native physics editor would write المؤثر القابل للرصد أو الكمية المرصودة. "informationally complete" is rendered المكتملة إعلامياً, where إعلامياً means "media-wise / publicity-wise" in modern usage rather than معلوماتياً; and the spelled-out POVM at line 84 (قياس إيجابي لعوامل تشغيل قيّمة مكتملة إعلامياً) scrambles "positive operator-valued measure" into something that reads as "positive measurement of valuable operating-factors" — recognizable only because the IC-POVM acronym sits next to it. Smaller: the mathematical "map" is consistently خريطة (a chart) instead of تحويل/تطبيق, "operator" splits between عوامل تشغيل (line 84) and العامل (line 182), the bullet-4 heading Measurement error mitigation is narrowed to تخفيف أخطاء القراءة (readout), and line 56 has a gender-agreement slip يشير تكلفة القياس (should be تشير).

examples.source: the expectation values of observables ... unbiased estimators for the observables
examples.suggested: القيم التوقعية للمؤثرات القابلة للرصد ... مقدِّرات غير متحيزة للمؤثرات القابلة للرصد
examples.translation: القيم التوقعية للمراقِبات ... مقدِّرات غير متحيزة للمراقِبات
examples.why: مراقِب with kasra is the active participle "observer" (the one who observes), inverting agent and patient: an observable is the observed quantity, not an observer. Used consistently 6 times, so the concept stays trackable from context, but a native technical editor would replace it with المؤثر القابل للرصد / الكمية المرصودة.

examples.source: measured with an informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (IC-POVM)
examples.suggested: مقياس ذو قيم مؤثِّرة موجبة ومكتمل معلوماتياً (IC-POVM)
examples.translation: قياس إيجابي لعوامل تشغيل قيّمة مكتملة إعلامياً (IC-POVM)
examples.why: The English compound is calqued word-by-word into a phrase that parses in Arabic as "a positive measurement of valuable operating-factors": قيّمة reads as "valuable" rather than "-valued", and عوامل تشغيل is the everyday "operating factors" not the mathematical مؤثِّرات. Only the adjacent IC-POVM acronym keeps it identifiable.

examples.source: informationally complete measurement outcomes / informationally complete measurements
examples.suggested: القياسات المكتملة معلوماتياً
examples.translation: نتائج القياسات المكتملة إعلامياً / القياسات المكتملة إعلامياً
examples.why: إعلامياً means "media-wise / in terms of publicity" in contemporary usage; the intended sense — complete with respect to information about the state — is معلوماتياً. Consistent across the file, so recognizable, but it is the wrong lexical root.

examples.source: build a noise-inversion map. The function applies a map that fully inverts the whole noisy circuit
examples.suggested: وبناء تحويل عكس الضوضاء. تطبّق الدالة تحويلاً يعكس الدائرة المشوَّشة بالكامل
examples.translation: وبناء خريطة عكس الضوضاء. تطبّق الدالة خريطة تعكس الدائرة المضطربة بالكامل
examples.why: خريطة is a geographic chart; the mathematical "map" is تحويل or تطبيق. Context ("applies a map that inverts the circuit") keeps the meaning inferable, so this is stylistic rather than misleading, but it is not what an Arabic-speaking physicist would write.

examples.source: The measurement overhead refers to the number of additional measurements required
examples.suggested: تشير تكلفة القياس إلى عدد القياسات الإضافية المطلوبة
examples.translation: يشير تكلفة القياس إلى عدد القياسات الإضافية المطلوبة
examples.why: Gender-agreement slip: تكلفة is feminine, so the verb must be تشير, not يشير — a residue of the English word order that a native writer would not produce.

editor_note: The closing sentence of the e-bit example inserts معاً ("together"), turning the English "the reduced state of BOTH Alice's qubit AND Bob's qubit is the completely mixed state" (i.e. each marginal ρ_A = ρ_B = I/2) into "the reduced state of Alice's qubit and Bob's qubit TOGETHER is the completely mixed state" — a claim about ρ_AB, which for a Bell state is the pure state |φ⁺⟩⟨φ⁺|, not I/4. This is misleading precisely at the joint-vs-marginal distinction the whole lesson teaches, and the later section (ρ_AC = Tr_B(ρ), "we can put the names of whatever systems we choose in the subscript") makes the false joint reading fully live rather than merely ambiguous. Everything else is sound: core terms are correct and consistent (density matrix→مصفوفة الكثافة, partial trace→الأثر الجزئي, traced out→يُحذف بالأثر, completely mixed state→الحالة المختلطة التامة, separable→قابلة للفصل, qubit→كيوبت), informal register holds (تذكّر). Remaining defects are minor: "possibility" rendered as احتمالية (probability) in the "nothing says Bob must measure" paragraph, the stiff calque المجموعات (ensemble) من الحالات الكمومية, and two gender-agreement slips (تصفها متجه الحالة, تُستخدم أحياناً حرف علوي).

examples.source: Indeed, for all four Bell states we find that the reduced state of both Alice's qubit and Bob's qubit is the completely mixed state.
examples.suggested: وبالفعل، لجميع حالات بيل الأربع نجد أن الحالة المختزلة لكلٍّ من كيوبت أليس وكيوبت بوب هي الحالة المختلطة التامة.
examples.translation: وبالفعل، لجميع حالات بيل الأربع نجد أن الحالة المختزلة لكيوبت أليس وكيوبت بوب معاً هي الحالة المختلطة التامة.
examples.why: معاً converts the English distributive "both … and …" (each marginal separately = I/2) into a statement about the JOINT reduced state ρ_AB, which for any Bell state is the pure state |φ⁺⟩⟨φ⁺| — the exact opposite of maximally mixed. The file later introduces exactly this multi-system subscript notation (ρ_AC = Tr_B(ρ)), so the false joint reading is a natural one and teaches a wrong concept about entangled pure states having mixed marginals.

examples.source: What we've done is to use the possibility that Bob measures his qubit to argue that the completely mixed state arises as the state of Alice's qubit
examples.suggested: ما فعلناه هو الاستعانة بإمكانية أن يقيس بوب كيوبته للاستدلال على أن حالة كيوبت أليس هي الحالة المختلطة التامة
examples.translation: ما فعلناه هو استخدام احتمالية أن يقيس بوب كيوبته كحجة على ظهور الحالة المختلطة التامة كحالة كيوبت أليس
examples.why: "Possibility" is rendered as احتمالية, which in this text is the established word for numerical probability (باحتمالية 1/2 appears repeatedly a few lines earlier). The correct word is إمكانية; as written it hints at a probability of Bob measuring, which is not part of the argument.

examples.source: Ensembles of quantum states.
examples.suggested: مجموعات (ensembles) من الحالات الكمومية.
examples.translation: المجموعات (ensemble) من الحالات الكمومية.
examples.why: Definite المجموعات followed by a partitive من is un-Arabic here and the parenthetical gloss is left singular against a plural head; a native technical writer would use the indefinite plural (or التجميعات الإحصائية). Stiff calque of the English list header rather than idiomatic Arabic.

editor_note: Faithful and natively phrased throughout; the blocking-call nuance is preserved exactly ("job.result() es una llamada bloqueante hasta que el job se complete"), retired QPUs is correctly expanded as "QPUs (unidades de procesamiento cuántico) retiradas", job/backend/runtime/Sampler/execution spans are consistently kept in English while "workload" is consistently "carga de trabajo", and the informal tú imperative holds everywhere (Consulta, Ve, Ten en cuenta, Usa, Prueba).

The math-bearing prose is faithful throughout — probabilities, the completely-mixed-state argument, the spectral-theorem derivation and the trace argument all track the English exactly, and core terms (matriz de densidad, estados puros, base ortonormal, valores propios / vectores propios, traza, positiva semidefinida) are correct and consistent. The one real terminology defect is "las matrices de densidad son siempre herméticas" (ES ~line 286): "hermética" means airtight/sealed; the domain term is "hermíticas" (or "hermitianas"). Secondary: "Propiedad ciclica de la traza" is missing its accent ("cíclica"), and the English sentence-initial "For example, because {|+>,|->} is an orthonormal basis…" is re-ordered so "por ejemplo" lands at the very end of the clause ("…en el segundo procedimiento es, por ejemplo,") right before a display equation, which reads as if the value itself were an example. Also "In words, normal matrices are…" became "Las matrices normales son, por tanto, matrices que conmutan…", turning a restatement into a deduction, and "This is a feature, not a bug!" loses its exclamation. None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the math.

examples.source: We can apply the spectral theorem to any given density matrix $\rho$ because density matrices are always Hermitian and therefore normal.
examples.suggested: …porque las matrices de densidad son siempre hermíticas y, por tanto, normales.
examples.translation: Podemos aplicar el teorema espectral a cualquier matriz de densidad $\rho$ dada, porque las matrices de densidad son siempre herméticas y, por tanto, normales.
examples.why: "Hermética" is an existing Spanish word meaning airtight/sealed — it is not the linear-algebra term. The conventional rendering of Hermitian is "hermítica" (or "hermitiana"); the current form teaches the learner a wrong label for the property, even though the logic Hermitian ⇒ normal survives intact.

examples.source: For example, because $\{\vert + \rangle, \vert - \rangle\}$ is an orthonormal basis, the probability to obtain the measurement outcome $0$ in the second procedure is
examples.suggested: Por ejemplo, como $\{\vert + \rangle, \vert - \rangle\}$ es una base ortonormal, la probabilidad de obtener el resultado de medición $0$ en el segundo procedimiento es
examples.translation: Como $\{\vert + \rangle, \vert - \rangle\}$ es una base ortonormal, la probabilidad de obtener el resultado de medición $0$ en el segundo procedimiento es, por ejemplo,
examples.why: Moving "por ejemplo" to the end of the clause, immediately before the display equation, makes it modify the value rather than introduce the case; a native technical writer would keep it sentence-initial as in the English.

examples.source: In words, normal matrices are matrices that commute with their own conjugate transpose.
examples.suggested: En otras palabras, las matrices normales son las que conmutan con su propia traspuesta conjugada.
examples.translation: Las matrices normales son, por tanto, matrices que conmutan con su propia traspuesta conjugada.
examples.why: "Por tanto" frames the sentence as an inference drawn from the definition, whereas the English explicitly marks it as a plain-language restatement of the same definition — the pedagogical signposting ("here is the same thing in words") is lost.

examples.source: Cyclic property of the trace:
examples.suggested: Propiedad cíclica de la traza:
examples.translation: Propiedad ciclica de la traza:
examples.why: Missing accent on "cíclica" in a theorem-box title — a visible orthographic slip in a heading a reader lands on directly.

editor_note: No semantic drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: every prose paragraph matches the English (the four `job.status()` states, the "1024 bytes in a kilobyte…" memory arithmetic, the two `/data` limitations — flat storage, only `tar`/`h5` — and the 16 cores / 32 GB program allocation are all faithfully carried over), and the informal "tú" register holds throughout ("puedes gestionar", "Asegúrate", "Recuerda", "Consulta", "Lee"). Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) In the Next-steps admonition, "quantum-centric supercomputing" is rendered as "la supercomputación cuántica centrada en quantum" — a garbled half-translation that leaves the English word "quantum" stranded and duplicates the adjective; the conventional Spanish is "supercomputación centrada en lo cuántico". (2) The `@distribute_task` paragraph reads as calqued English: "esto crea una tarea de trabajador paralelo asíncrona con un único núcleo de CPU" stacks three adjectives on "tarea" with a gender/agreement stumble ("trabajador paralelo … asíncrona") that no Spanish technical writer would produce; "tarea paralela asíncrona en un worker/proceso de trabajo" is the natural phrasing. Neither issue would make a learner form a false belief, so this is not a FAIL despite the fast pass's verdict.

examples.source: Read a paper in which researchers used Qiskit Serverless and quantum-centric supercomputing to explore quantum chemistry.
examples.suggested: Lee un artículo en el que unos investigadores usaron Qiskit Serverless y la supercomputación centrada en lo cuántico para explorar la química cuántica.
examples.translation: Lee un artículo en el que investigadores usaron Qiskit Serverless y la supercomputación cuántica centrada en quantum para explorar la química cuántica.
examples.why: "centrada en quantum" leaves the English head noun untranslated inside a Spanish noun phrase and duplicates the adjective ("cuántica … quantum"). The established Spanish rendering of quantum-centric supercomputing is "supercomputación centrada en lo cuántico". Recognizable, so MINOR, but it reads as an unfinished translation in the one paragraph a reader is most likely to click through from.

examples.source: When run, this creates an asynchronous parallel worker task with a single CPU core, and returns with a reference to track the worker.
examples.suggested: Al ejecutarse, esto crea una tarea paralela asíncrona en un proceso de trabajo con un único núcleo de CPU y devuelve una referencia para hacer el seguimiento de ese proceso.
examples.translation: Al ejecutarse, esto crea una tarea de trabajador paralelo asíncrona con un único núcleo de CPU, y devuelve una referencia para rastrear el trabajador.
examples.why: Calqued English noun stacking: "tarea de trabajador paralelo asíncrona" forces the reader to guess whether "paralelo" modifies "trabajador" and "asíncrona" modifies "tarea" — the agreement endings contradict the intended reading. Meaning survives, but it is textbook translationese rather than something a Spanish-speaking engineer would write.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing sentence (property 1's "si y solo si", property 3's "no decrece bajo la acción de cualquier canal", the ε-conditions "> 1 - \varepsilon", the Fuchs-van de Graaf reading of the figure, and the Uhlmann *máximo* statement) and found no drift, no inversion and no hallucination; informal "tú" holds ("observa primero", "tómate un momento"). The problems are orthographic and stylistic. First, a systematic accent-stripping affects at least eight words: "enigmatica"/"quizas" (l.26), "cual definición" (l.40), "maximo" (ll.90, 239, 246), "menciono" (l.108), "imagenes" (l.120), "ademas" (l.262), "varian"/"varia" (l.314). Two of these are real word errors, not just missing tildes: "aplicando está definición" (l.82) and "A partir de está observación" (l.180) write the verb *está* where the demonstrative *esta* is required. Second, "positive semidefinite" is consistently rendered with English word order as "positiva semidefinida" instead of the standard Spanish "semidefinida positiva", and "a basic way to measure their similarity" is upgraded to "una forma fundamental" (l.18) while the parallel "basic measure" three lines later is correctly "medida básica" (l.21). None of this misleads a learner, but all of it is what a native technical editor would fix.

examples.source: and by applying this definition to the matrix …  /  From this observation we can conclude …
examples.suggested: y aplicando esta definición a la matriz …  /  A partir de esta observación, podemos concluir …
examples.translation: y aplicando está definición a la matriz …  /  A partir de está observación, podemos concluir …
examples.why: *está* is the third-person verb 'is'; the demonstrative adjective is *esta* (no accent). Written as-is the phrase is ungrammatical ('applying it-is definition'), and it occurs twice, so it reads as an uncorrected MT artifact rather than a typo.

examples.source: unusual or mysterious, and perhaps not easy to work with / Here the maximum is over … / as was mentioned at the start of the section / orthogonal images / We'll also define / As U and V range over …
examples.suggested: enigmática … quizás / el máximo / como se mencionó / imágenes ortogonales / Definimos además / varían … varía
examples.translation: inusual o enigmatica, y quizas no fácil de manejar / Aquí el maximo se toma … / como se menciono al inicio de la sección / imagenes ortogonales / Definimos ademas / U y V varian … también varia …
examples.why: A systematic loss of diacritics across the file. 'menciono' (I mention) vs 'mencionó' (was mentioned) and 'varia' vs 'varía' are different words, not just misspellings, so a careful reader stumbles; a Spanish-speaking technical writer would never leave these.

examples.source: one must always be careful to understand or clarify which definition is being used.
examples.suggested: siempre hay que tener cuidado de entender o aclarar qué definición se está utilizando.
examples.translation: siempre hay que tener cuidado de entender o aclarar cual definición se está utilizando.
examples.why: 'cual definición' is a calque of English 'which definition'; before a noun Spanish uses *qué* (and if *cuál* were used at all it would need its accent). Reads as translationese in an otherwise fluent paragraph.

examples.source: positive semidefinite matrix
examples.suggested: matriz semidefinida positiva
examples.translation: matriz positiva semidefinida
examples.why: The established Spanish linear-algebra term is 'semidefinida positiva'; the translation keeps English adjective order. It is consistent within the file and still recognizable, so it is a calque rather than a false concept — but it is the term a Spanish textbook would use differently.

examples.source: This provides a basic way to measure their similarity
examples.suggested: Esto proporciona una forma básica de medir su similitud
examples.translation: Esto proporciona una forma fundamental de medir su similitud
examples.why: 'basic' here means rudimentary/elementary, and the very next paragraph translates the parallel 'basic measure of similarity' correctly as 'medida básica'. 'fundamental' mildly upgrades the claim and breaks the internal echo the English builds between the two sentences.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout: the removal caveat is rendered exactly ("sus cargas de trabajo y los resultados asociados dejan de ser visibles para él. Otros usuarios de la misma instancia aún pueden acceder..."), the numbered invite steps preserve every action and the "opcionalmente" qualifier, and informal tú is consistent (Crea / asegúrate / haz clic / Se te pedirá). Two small things a native technical editor would still touch: "Si un usuario ya tiene una cuenta de IBM Cloud existente" is pleonastic — "ya... existente" double-marks the same idea, a calque of "previously existing"; and in the tip block "a specific instance's access group" becomes "un grupo de acceso específico de esa instancia", which moves "específico" from the instance onto the group, subtly suggesting a choice among several groups of one instance rather than the group belonging to a specific instance. Neither would mislead a reader about how the product works, so this stays MINOR; terminology (instancia, grupo de acceso, Gestión de acceso, cargas de trabajo) is correct and consistent file-wide.

examples.source: If a user has a previously existing IBM Cloud account, follow the instructions in the [Manage IBM Cloud users] section.
examples.suggested: Si un usuario ya tiene una cuenta de IBM Cloud, sigue las instrucciones en la sección [Gestionar usuarios de IBM Cloud].
examples.translation: Si un usuario ya tiene una cuenta de IBM Cloud existente, sigue las instrucciones en la sección [Gestionar usuarios de IBM Cloud].
examples.why: "ya tiene ... existente" is redundant in Spanish — "ya" already carries "previously existing". A native writer would drop "existente"; keeping both reads as a word-for-word calque of the English.

examples.source: When you invite users to an instance, you can assign them to a specific instance's access group as part of the invitation process.
examples.suggested: Al invitar usuarios a una instancia, puedes asignarlos al grupo de acceso de esa instancia concreta como parte del proceso de invitación.
examples.translation: Al invitar usuarios a una instancia, puedes asignarlos a un grupo de acceso específico de esa instancia como parte del proceso de invitación.
examples.why: The modifier "specific" belongs to the instance in English (the access group of a given instance); the Spanish attaches "específico" to the group, implying a selection among several access groups within one instance. The preceding sentence says one group is auto-generated per instance, so the emphasis is slightly off — no practical consequence for the reader, hence minor.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the factorial/exponential scaling examples (50 partículas, 10.000 ciudades, "órdenes de magnitud más tiempo que la edad actual de nuestro sol"), the QCSC three-tier hardware list, and the "no existe un buen equivalente cuántico de la RAM" passage all track the English exactly, and core terms are correct and consistent (puertas y circuitos cuánticos, entrelazamiento, superposición, mitigación de errores, tolerantes a fallos); informal "tú" holds everywhere ("proporcionarte", "consulta", "Considera este curso"). What a native editor would fix: two real misspellings, "HPC evoluciónó hacia la computación paralela" and "Esta lección proporciónó contexto" (should be "evolucionó" / "proporcionó"), plus a relative-pronoun slip in "construido por Seymour Cray, quien a menudo se le llama el padre de la supercomputación" (needs "a quien ... se le llama"). Two renderings are calques a Spanish HPC writer would not use: "la manipulación de tales enormes volúmenes de datos" (natural order: "volúmenes de datos tan enormes") and "interconexiones de tiempo cercano" for "near-time interconnects". One qualifier is dropped: "a few words on Slurm" becomes "y explica Slurm", overstating what the guide offers; and "commodity hardware" is rendered "hardware comercial" (commodity = de uso común/estándar), though the following gloss "servidores comunes" rescues it. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: HPC evolved toward parallel computing
examples.suggested: HPC evolucionó hacia la computación paralela
examples.translation: HPC evoluciónó hacia la computación paralela
examples.why: Misspelling: stray accent on the stem. Same defect recurs at the course outline: "proporciónó" should be "proporcionó".

examples.source: built by Seymour Cray, often referred to as the father of supercomputing
examples.suggested: construido por Seymour Cray, a quien a menudo se le llama el padre de la supercomputación
examples.translation: construido por Seymour Cray, quien a menudo se le llama el padre de la supercomputación
examples.why: Ungrammatical relative clause: "quien" as subject clashes with the clitic "se le"; a native writer uses "a quien ... se le llama" or "a menudo llamado".

examples.source: it covers the SPANK plugin for the quantum resource management and a few words on Slurm
examples.suggested: ...y dedica unas palabras a Slurm
examples.translation: cubre el plugin SPANK para la gestión de recursos cuánticos y explica Slurm
examples.why: The English qualifier "a few words" is dropped, so the Spanish promises a full explanation of Slurm where the source promises only a passing mention.

examples.source: manipulating such vast amounts of data already consumes megawatts of power
examples.suggested: manipular volúmenes de datos tan enormes ya consume megavatios de energía
examples.translation: la manipulación de tales enormes volúmenes de datos ya consume megavatios de energía
examples.why: "tales enormes" is a word-for-word calque of "such vast"; Spanish puts the intensifier after the noun ("tan enormes") and prefers the infinitive over the nominalization here.

examples.source: HPC moved toward clusters of commodity hardware
examples.suggested: clústeres de hardware de uso común / hardware estándar
examples.translation: HPC se desplazó hacia clústeres de hardware comercial
examples.why: "commodity hardware" means off-the-shelf, standard components, not "commercial" hardware; the following gloss "servidores comunes" keeps it recoverable, so this is imperfect rather than misleading.

examples.source: connected via near-time interconnects for tasks like error mitigation
examples.suggested: conectados mediante interconexiones de baja latencia (near-time)
examples.translation: conectados mediante interconexiones de tiempo cercano para tareas como la mitigación de errores
examples.why: "de tiempo cercano" is a literal rendering that means nothing in Spanish HPC usage; either keep the English term or paraphrase the latency notion.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: every prose claim matches the source (e.g. "Los usuarios del plan Open no pueden enviar jobs de sesión", "El modo batch puede ayudar a reducir el tiempo de procesamiento si todos los jobs pueden proporcionarse desde el principio"), "context manager" → "gestor de contexto" and "broadcasting de numpy" are the right conventions, and informal "tú" (Puedes, Consulta, Empieza, Revisa, Practica) holds from first line to the Recomendaciones block; the English API-mode tokens (job/session/batch) are kept deliberately to match the `mode` payload values and are used consistently.

Semantically faithful throughout — the load-bearing technical claims all survive intact: black/white tiles map correctly to X/Z stabilizer generators, the X-chain = left-to-right / Z-chain = top-to-bottom distinction is preserved, "encodes a single qubit, rather than two" and the gross-code figures ([[144,12,12]], weight 6, 12 vs. two logical qubits) are all correct, and the three-colouring condition ("ningún par de caras del mismo color compartan una arista") is rendered exactly. What a native technical editor would still change is surface polish: two English calques survive verbatim ("Como resulta ser" for "As it turns out", where Spanish wants "Resulta que"/"De hecho"; and "arañar la superficie" where the fixed Spanish idiom is "rascar la superficie"), "so-called rough edges" is word-ordered as "bordes llamados rugosos" instead of the natural "los llamados bordes rugosos", and one sentence mixes two constructions ungrammatically: "Para quienes deseen profundizar más, pueden consultar…" (either "Quienes deseen… pueden consultar" or "Para quienes deseen…, está el Zoo"). Terminology is consistent — "generadores de estabilizadores", "código tórico", "código de superficie", "baldosas", qubit kept in English — though "lattice" → "cuadrícula" is weaker than the conventional "red"/"retícula" for a code lattice. None of this misleads a learner.

examples.source: As it turns out, it isn't actually necessary that the toric code has periodic boundaries.
examples.suggested: Resulta que el código tórico no necesita tener bordes periódicos.
examples.translation: Como resulta ser, el código tórico no necesita tener bordes periódicos.
examples.why: "Como resulta ser" is a word-for-word calque of "As it turns out" and is not idiomatic Spanish; a native technical writer would open with "Resulta que" or "De hecho". Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: but we will scratch the surface just a bit to briefly examine a couple of prominent examples
examples.suggested: pero al menos rascaremos la superficie para examinar brevemente un par de ejemplos destacados
examples.translation: pero queremos al menos arañar la superficie y considerar brevemente dos ejemplos prominentes
examples.why: The fixed Spanish idiom is "rascar la superficie"; "arañar la superficie" reads as a literal rendering of the English metaphor rather than the established expression.

examples.source: Those interested in exploring deeper may wish to consult the Error Correction Zoo
examples.suggested: Quienes deseen profundizar más pueden consultar el Error Correction Zoo
examples.translation: Para quienes deseen profundizar más, pueden consultar el Error Correction Zoo
examples.why: Ungrammatical blend: the preposition "Para" turns the relative clause into an adjunct, leaving "pueden consultar" without a subject. Drop "Para" (or recast the main clause).

examples.source: where the lattice is cut with so-called rough edges at the top and bottom
examples.suggested: donde la red se corta con los llamados bordes rugosos en la parte superior e inferior
examples.translation: donde la cuadrícula tiene bordes llamados rugosos en la parte superior e inferior
examples.why: Two slips in one clause: "bordes llamados rugosos" mis-orders the "so-called" marker (Spanish puts it before the noun: "los llamados bordes rugosos"), and "cuadrícula" (grid) is a weaker rendering of the code "lattice" than "red"/"retícula". Also loses the sense that the lattice is *cut*.

examples.source: Recall that the stabilizer generators for this code are as follows.
examples.suggested: Recuerda que los generadores de estabilizadores para este código son los siguientes.
examples.translation: Los generadores de estabilizadores para este código son los siguientes.
examples.why: The "Recall that" cue is dropped, flattening the pedagogical signal that this is a callback to material the learner has already seen rather than a new definition. Not misleading, but the teaching emphasis is weaker than the English.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every migration claim, negation, version number and support date matches the English (c_if removal, `Instruction.duration`/`unit` removal, the six `generate_preset_pass_manager` items, "bug-fix support until September 2024 / security support until March 2025"), and the informal "tú" register holds throughout ("Usa la tabla de contenidos", "Ten en cuenta", "Debes usar"). Domain terms are correct and consistent (gate→compuerta, transpilación/transpilador, pasadas del transpilador, qubits/target/backend kept in English). What a native technical editor would change: an outright spelling error "si no se proporciónó" (double accent, should be "proporcionó"); the repeated anglicism "ya no está soportado" / "soportada por hardware" where Spanish technical writing uses "ya no es compatible" / "compatible con el hardware"; "Esto retornará" instead of "Esto devolverá"; and the calqued passive "los supuestos bajo los cuales es válido serán violados con mayor frecuencia", which also flattens the English intensifier "more and more". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: or `None`, if not supplied
examples.suggested: o `None`, si no se proporcionó
examples.translation: o `None`, si no se proporciónó
examples.why: Outright orthographic error: the accent is on the wrong syllable and duplicated ("proporciónó"). Purely mechanical, but a native editor fixes it on sight.

examples.source: The `backend_properties` input argument is no longer supported / a particular hardware-supported `Instruction`
examples.suggested: El argumento de entrada `backend_properties` ya no es compatible / una `Instruction` compatible con el hardware
examples.translation: El argumento de entrada `backend_properties` ya no está soportado / una `Instruction` particular soportada por hardware
examples.why: "soportado" for "supported" is a well-known English calque; Spanish technical documentation uses "compatible con" (or "ya no se admite"). It recurs three times, so it reads as MT habit rather than a one-off.

examples.source: the assumptions under which it is valid will be violated more and more frequently
examples.suggested: los supuestos en los que se basa se incumplirán cada vez más a menudo
examples.translation: los supuestos bajo los cuales es válido serán violados con mayor frecuencia
examples.why: Calqued English passive ("serán violados") plus loss of the escalating "more and more" — "con mayor frecuencia" states a single comparison rather than a growing trend. Meaning survives; the emphasis is flattened.

examples.source: This will return either `None` ... or an `InstructionProperties` instance
examples.suggested: Esto devolverá `None` ... o bien una instancia de `InstructionProperties`
examples.translation: Esto retornará ya sea `None` ... o una instancia de `InstructionProperties`
examples.why: "retornar" is an anglicism in this sense (Spanish uses "devolver" for a function return value), and "ya sea ... o" copies the English "either ... or" scaffolding word for word.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every quantitative claim survives intact — the nested double-negative in "si con una probabilidad de como máximo 1/2 no obtenemos la cadena única… no habremos obtenido esta cadena única x con una probabilidad de como máximo 2^{-m}" is correct, the catastrophic-overrotation passage ("pasamos de largo el objetivo |A_1⟩ y terminamos cerca de −|A_0⟩") is faithful, and the peculiar-bound caveat ("más soluciones implican una peor cota inferior") and the t=0 aside ("con t=0 es exactamente la adivinación aleatoria") are both preserved. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: "obtenemos garantizadamente un resultado de medición" uses a non-idiomatic adverb where Spanish wants "tenemos la garantía de obtener"; "Supongamos que no supiéramos nada mejor" is a word-for-word calque of "didn't know any better" that reads as English syntax; "el número de elementos sobre los que estamos buscando" mis-selects the preposition (buscar entre, not sobre); and "como los valores anteriores parecen confirmar" nudges "seem to suggest" toward confirmation. Register is consistently informal (Observa, Concentrémonos, Examinemos) and domain terms (cota inferior, adivinación aleatoria, consultas, cadena, medición) are correct and consistent throughout.

examples.source: for if we measure this state, we're guaranteed to get a measurement outcome $x\in A_1.$
examples.suggested: porque, al medir este estado, tenemos la garantía de obtener un resultado de medición $x\in A_1$.
examples.translation: porque al medir este estado, obtenemos garantizadamente un resultado de medición $x\in A_1$.
examples.why: "garantizadamente" is a dictionary-legal but essentially unused adverb in Spanish technical prose; it marks the sentence as machine-produced where a native writer would use "tenemos la garantía de" or "con certeza obtendremos".

examples.source: Suppose that we didn't know any better, and selected the same value of $t$ as in the unique solution setting:
examples.suggested: Supongamos que, por desconocimiento, eligiéramos el mismo valor de $t$ que en el caso de solución única:
examples.translation: Supongamos que no supiéramos nada mejor y eligiéramos el mismo valor de $t$ que en el caso de solución única:
examples.why: "no supiéramos nada mejor" is a literal calque of the English idiom "didn't know any better" and has no idiomatic force in Spanish; the reader has to back-translate it to parse the setup of the catastrophic-failure example.

examples.source: The first argument, $N,$ refers to the number of items we're searching over
examples.suggested: El primer argumento, $N$, se refiere al número de elementos entre los que buscamos
examples.translation: El primer argumento, $N$, se refiere al número de elementos sobre los que estamos buscando
examples.why: The English particle "searching over" is carried across as "buscar sobre", which is not the Spanish collocation (one busca entre elementos, or busca en un conjunto); the calqued preposition is the giveaway.

examples.source: so the probability of success goes to $1$ in the limit as $N$ becomes large, as the values above seem to suggest.
examples.suggested: …como parecen sugerir los valores anteriores.
examples.translation: de modo que la probabilidad de éxito tiende a $1$ en el límite de $N$ grande, como los valores anteriores parecen confirmar.
examples.why: "suggest" is deliberately weak here — the table is evidence, the proof is what establishes the bound. "parecen confirmar" upgrades tabulated data to confirmation of a theorem; the hedge "parecen" keeps it from misleading, so this is minor, but the epistemic emphasis of the teaching sentence is flattened.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination; quantities (`1024`/`1000` shots, `900` randomisations, 10 ensembles, trois instructions uniques) and conditions all match, and "up to single-qubit gates" is well rendered as "à des gates à un qubit près". The defects are lexical and stylistic: "probabilistic error cancellation" becomes "la cancellation d'erreurs probabiliste" — "cancellation" is not a French word (standard is "annulation probabiliste d'erreurs"); and "mitigate/mitigation" is rendered with the anglicisms "mitiger"/"mitigation" ("que nous voulons mitiger avec PEC", "la mitigation d'erreurs") where French quantum docs say "atténuer"/"atténuation". The file also mixes instruction moods: it addresses the reader with tutoiement ("tu dois installer", "Tu peux le faire manuellement", "Consulte", "Apprends") but renders nearly every step instruction as a bare infinitive ("Préparer un état GHZ…", "Choisir un backend…", "Initialiser un programme vide"), so the same document teaches in two voices. Minor calques remain ("Également demander `900` randomisations", "L'utilisation pour cet exemple est d'environ 10 minutes" for QPU usage time, "fonction de commodité").

examples.source: perform probabilistic error cancellation ([PEC](...)) for error mitigation
examples.suggested: effectuer l'annulation probabiliste d'erreurs ([PEC](...)) pour l'atténuation des erreurs
examples.translation: effectuer la cancellation d'erreurs probabiliste ([PEC](...)) pour la mitigation d'erreurs
examples.why: "cancellation" does not exist in French (the noun is "annulation"), and "mitigation" is an anglicism; the conventional French rendering of error mitigation is "atténuation des erreurs". Recognizable thanks to the PEC link, so not misleading, but a native editor would rewrite it.

examples.source: Learn: Learn the noise of the instructions that we want to mitigate with PEC.
examples.suggested: Apprentissage : apprendre le bruit des instructions que nous voulons atténuer avec la PEC.
examples.translation: Apprentissage : Apprendre le bruit des instructions que nous voulons mitiger avec PEC.
examples.why: French "mitiger" means to temper or moderate something (e.g. a judgement), not to reduce noise; "atténuer" is the term used in French quantum-computing writing.

examples.source: Prepare a three-qubit GHZ state… / Choose a backend… vs. you must install Samplomatic / You can do this manually
examples.suggested: Prépare un état GHZ à trois qubits… / Choisis un backend… (align the step instructions with the tutoiement used elsewhere)
examples.translation: Préparer un état GHZ à trois qubits… / Choisir un backend… vs. tu dois installer Samplomatic / Tu peux le faire manuellement
examples.why: The file commits to informal "tu" in explanatory prose and in the Next-steps list ("Consulte", "Apprends"), but renders the actual procedural steps as impersonal infinitives, so the tutorial speaks in two voices. Either convention alone is defensible; the mix is not.

examples.source: Also request `900` randomizations from the samplex.
examples.suggested: Demande également `900` randomisations au samplex.
examples.translation: Également demander `900` randomisations au samplex.
examples.why: Fronting "Également" before an infinitive is a direct calque of the English "Also request…"; no French technical writer opens a sentence this way.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every proof step (existence of purifications, Schmidt decomposition, unitary equivalence, bit-commitment impossibility, Hughston-Jozsa-Wootters) against the source and found no inversion, no swapped quantity, no dropped caveat and nothing hallucinated; core terminology is correct and consistent (matrice densité, trace partielle, décomposition spectrale, vecteurs propres, état complètement mélangé, matrices semi-définies positives, codage superdense, engagement de bit / contraignant / dissimulant), and the informal "tu" convention holds (Suppose que…, Considère…, Note que…). What a native technical editor would still change is translationese: "uniquement déterminé(s)" is used about six times as a calque of "uniquely determined" (French "uniquement" reads as "solely", the idiom is "déterminé de manière unique" — and the file already uses the better "une sélection unique" once, so it is internally inconsistent too); "il pourrait être que N = 1 000 000" is not idiomatic ("il se pourrait que"); and in the superdense-coding paragraph "pour savoir dans quel état de Bell il se trouve" attaches the pronoun to Bob rather than to the pair (A,B), literally saying Bob is in a Bell state. Two smaller points: "réels positifs" / "entier positif" drop the "strictement" that French convention needs (positif includes 0 in French, whereas Schmidt coefficients must be > 0), and the passive "lorsque Y est tracé" for "traced out" is thin next to "lorsqu'on prend la trace partielle sur Y". None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: which are uniquely determined (up to their ordering)
examples.suggested: qui sont déterminés de manière unique (à l'ordre près)
examples.translation: qui sont uniquement déterminés (à leur ordre près)
examples.why: Calque: French 'uniquement' means 'solely/only', so 'uniquement déterminé' reads as 'determined only'. Standard phrasing is 'déterminé de manière unique' / 'univoquement déterminé'. Recurs about six times, and line 172 already uses the better 'une sélection unique de vecteurs', so the file is inconsistent with itself.

examples.source: For instance, it could be that $N = 1,000,000$ while X and Y are qubits.
examples.suggested: Par exemple, il se pourrait que $N = 1\,000\,000$ alors que X et Y sont des qubits.
examples.translation: Par exemple, il pourrait être que $N = 1\,000\,000$ tandis que X et Y sont des qubits.
examples.why: 'il pourrait être que' is a word-for-word rendering of 'it could be that' and is not idiomatic French; the impersonal construction is 'il se pourrait que' (or simply 'on pourrait avoir N = …').

examples.source: then Bob performs a measurement on the pair (A,B) to see which Bell state he holds
examples.suggested: puis Bob effectue une mesure sur la paire (A,B) pour déterminer quel état de Bell il détient
examples.translation: puis Bob effectue une mesure sur la paire (A,B) pour savoir dans quel état de Bell il se trouve
examples.why: 'il se trouve' attaches to Bob (the only masculine antecedent — 'la paire' is feminine), so it literally says Bob is in a Bell state, whereas the English says he holds the state. Recoverable from context, but a native editor would fix the pronoun.

examples.source: where $p_0,\ldots,p_{r-1}$ are positive real numbers summing to 1
examples.suggested: où $p_0,\ldots,p_{r-1}$ sont des réels strictement positifs dont la somme vaut 1
examples.translation: où $p_0,\ldots,p_{r-1}$ sont des réels positifs dont la somme vaut 1
examples.why: In French convention 'positif' includes 0, so the qualifier that makes the Schmidt-decomposition definition work (all coefficients > 0 — exactly why the zero-eigenvalue terms are discarded later) is lost. Same gap in 'pour tout entier positif n' and 'un entier positif arbitraire' (English 'positive integer' = at least 1).

examples.source: that leaves $\rho$ when Y is traced out
examples.suggested: qui redonne $\rho$ lorsqu'on prend la trace partielle sur Y
examples.translation: qui redonne $\rho$ lorsque Y est tracé
examples.why: Bare passive 'est tracé' is ambiguous in French ('tracer' first reads as 'to plot/draw'); the field says 'prendre la trace partielle sur Y' or 'tracer sur les degrés de liberté de Y'. Same in the HJW proof: 'un seul système composé qu'on peut tracer pour laisser X'.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (six slices → six groups not eight, "dépasse huit", the anti-commutation example with $IZ$ requiring a separate basis, the noiseless-simulator caveat "la troncature dégrade le résultat en raison de l'approximation introduite", the $\simeq 0{,}89$ tensor-network reference value). Four editorial defects remain. (1) A real typo creating a non-word: "Nous transpitons maintenant les circuits original et rétropropagé" — should be "transpilons"; elsewhere the verb is correct ("Nous n'avons pas besoin de transpiler"). (2) The informal "tu" convention is broken repeatedly by vouvoyed imperatives: "Consultez la documentation", "Notez que dans un simulateur sans bruit", "consultez ce guide pratique", "Consultez également ce guide", against "assure-toi d'avoir installé", "Ci-dessous, tu verras", "Si tu as trouvé ce travail intéressant". (3) "observable" is treated as masculine throughout ("l'observable mesuré", "un observable à deux qubits", "du nouvel observable", "l'observable rétropropagé") where French quantum-mechanics usage is feminine ("une observable"). (4) "First" is rendered as the stiff "Premièrement" twice ("Premièrement, nous utiliserons la fonction…", "Premièrement, nous créons deux…") where a native technical writer would write "Tout d'abord".

examples.source: Now we transpile both the original and the backpropagated circuits into the basis gate of the backend.
examples.suggested: Nous transpilons maintenant les circuits original et rétropropagé dans la porte de base du backend.
examples.translation: Nous transpitons maintenant les circuits original et rétropropagé dans la porte de base du backend.
examples.why: "transpitons" is not a French word — the verb is "transpiler" ("nous transpilons"), and the same file uses it correctly in the very next sentence ("besoin de transpiler sur le backend réel"). A visible typo on a core domain verb.

examples.source: Note that in a noiseless simulator, the expectation value obtained with and without backpropagation will be same.
examples.suggested: Note que dans un simulateur sans bruit, la valeur attendue obtenue avec et sans rétropropagation sera la même.
examples.translation: Notez que dans un simulateur sans bruit, la valeur attendue obtenue avec et sans rétropropagation sera la même.
examples.why: The file otherwise uses informal "tu" ("assure-toi d'avoir installé", "Ci-dessous, tu verras", "Si tu as trouvé ce travail intéressant"), but four instructional imperatives are vouvoyed ("Notez", "Consultez" ×3). Register flips within the same page.

examples.source: …absorbing operations from the end of a quantum circuit into the measured observable…
examples.suggested: …absorber dans l'observable mesurée les opérations situées en fin de circuit quantique…
examples.translation: …absorber des opérations depuis la fin d'un circuit quantique dans l'observable mesuré…
examples.why: "observable" is inflected masculine throughout ("l'observable mesuré", "un observable à deux qubits", "du nouvel observable", "l'observable rétropropagé"); standard French quantum-mechanics usage is feminine ("une observable"). Consistent, so not misleading, but a native physicist would re-gender it.

examples.source: First, we shall use the generate_xyz_hamiltonian function… / First, we create two Primitive Unified Blocs (PUBs)…
examples.suggested: Tout d'abord, nous utiliserons la fonction generate_xyz_hamiltonian… / Nous commençons par créer deux Primitive Unified Blocs (PUBs)…
examples.translation: Premièrement, nous utiliserons la fonction generate_xyz_hamiltonian… / Premièrement, nous créons deux Primitive Unified Blocs (PUBs)…
examples.why: "Premièrement" is an enumerator used in argumentation (premièrement/deuxièmement), not the natural discourse opener for a tutorial step; French technical writing uses "Tout d'abord" or "Nous commençons par". Reads as a one-to-one calque of "First,".

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: every policy bullet, the four numbered console procedures, the permissions table (including the ✴️ "Dépend des paramètres de visibilité de l'utilisateur" dependency row and the ❌ for "Supprimer des charges de travail quantiques" for collaborators) and the role-action table all match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout. Role terminology is correct and consistent ("Rôle d'accès au service **Manager**" vs "Rôle d'accès à la gestion de la plateforme **Administrator**"), and UI labels are rendered consistently ("Attribuer un accès", "tickets de support"). Two purely editorial slips: the trailing brand attribution in "via la [console], la [CLI], l'[API] ou [Terraform] IBM Cloud®" is a calque of the English attributive stacking and momentarily reads as if "Terraform IBM Cloud" were a product; and "Dans le panneau gauche" is a stiff literalism where the file itself later uses the idiomatic "panneau de droite".

examples.source: You can create additional access groups by using the IBM Cloud console, CLI, API, or Terraform.
examples.suggested: Tu peux créer des groupes d'accès supplémentaires via la console IBM Cloud®, la CLI, l'API ou Terraform.
examples.translation: Tu peux créer des groupes d'accès supplémentaires via la [console], la [CLI], l'[API] ou [Terraform] IBM Cloud®.
examples.why: English stacks the brand once in front of a list of attributive nouns; French cannot carry that attribution across a coordinated list from the tail. As written, 'Terraform IBM Cloud' reads as a single product name. Attaching 'IBM Cloud' to the first item is both idiomatic and unambiguous.

examples.source: On the left panel in the **Manage access** section, click **Access groups**
examples.suggested: Dans le panneau de gauche, sous la section **Gérer l'accès**, clique sur **Groupes d'accès**
examples.translation: Dans le panneau gauche, sous la section **Gérer l'accès**, clique sur **Groupes d'accès**
examples.why: 'panneau gauche' is a bare calque of 'left panel'; French UI prose uses 'panneau de gauche'. The same file already writes 'panneau de droite' a few lines later, so the two are inconsistent with each other as well.

editor_note: No misleading content: every technical claim (circuit depth as the minimum number of parallel gate layers, the depth "game", resilience levels 0/1/2, ZNE adding noise to extrapolate backwards, PEC being off the 3rd level and manually enabled, PEA "not yet in Qiskit") is faithfully rendered, and the informal "tu" holds throughout. The defects are terminological/stylistic: Qiskit's "job" is rendered "un emploi plus grand" (the employment sense — should be "tâche/job"); "shots" becomes "(ou coups)" and "Pauli twirling" becomes "tourbillonnement de Pauli", both over-translations of terms the French Qiskit community keeps in English (note the file itself keeps "Twirled Readout Error eXtinction" untranslated two paragraphs later); and SWAP gates are called "portes SWAP" in the Optimize section but "portes de permutation" in the transpiler routing step. Two small slips: "make sure everything is lined up the way you would expect" is weakened to "comme tu le souhaites" (as you wish), and "décoherence" is missing its accent ("décohérence"). A few calques remain ("un problème relativement large" for a large problem, "le signal… coule dans la ligne de transmission", "une suggestion informée").

examples.source: A primitive is a small building block that you can use to design a larger circuit or job.
examples.suggested: … pour concevoir un circuit ou une tâche (job) plus vaste.
examples.translation: Une primitive est un petit bloc de construction que tu peux utiliser pour concevoir un circuit ou un emploi plus grand.
examples.why: "emploi" is the employment sense of "job"; the Qiskit concept of a submitted job is "tâche"/"job". The phrase reads as nonsense to a French quantum engineer.

examples.source: Pauli twirling
examples.suggested: le twirling de Pauli
examples.translation: le tourbillonnement de Pauli
examples.why: French quantum literature keeps "twirling"; "tourbillonnement" is a literal calque that makes the technique hard to recognize — especially since the very next paragraph keeps "Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (T-REX)" in English. Consistent within the file, so recognizable, but not the field's term.

examples.source: The more runs (or shots) it performs, the more accurate the results will be
examples.suggested: Plus il effectue d'exécutions (ou shots), plus les résultats seront précis
examples.translation: Plus il effectue d'exécutions (ou coups), plus les résultats seront précis
examples.why: "shots" is kept in English in French Qiskit usage (it is the API parameter name); "coups" is a literal rendering that a learner will not connect to the `shots` argument they will type.

examples.source: injects gates (such as swap gates) … / Try to avoid too many costly SWAP gates.
examples.suggested: injecte des portes (telles que des portes SWAP)
examples.translation: injecte des portes (telles que des portes de permutation) … / Essaie d'éviter trop de portes SWAP coûteuses.
examples.why: Same gate rendered two ways within the file — "portes SWAP" in the Optimize section, "portes de permutation" in the routing stage. Both are intelligible, but the split obscures that the routing stage inserts exactly the costly gates warned about earlier.

examples.source: …and make sure everything is lined up the way you would expect.
